sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.code: fapolicyd [options]

sections.title: DESCRIPTION
sections.code:
fapolicyd is a userspace daemon that determines access rights to
files based on a trust database and file or process attributes. It
supports both blacklist and whitelist approaches to file access and
execution control.

Configuration is spread across three files in /etc/fapolicyd/:
compiled.rules (the access policy, generated by fagenrules from
rules.d/), fapolicyd.conf (daemon configuration), and
fapolicyd.trust (administrator-defined trusted files).

The default rules generate audit events for denials; at least one
audit rule must be loaded for a complete FANOTIFY event. Check for
denials with:
ausearch --start today -m fanotify -i

sections.title: OPTIONS
sections.code:
--debug
    Stay in the foreground for debugging, writing event information to
    stderr so policy decisions can be observed directly.

--debug-deny
    Foreground debugging mode, but only denied decisions are written
    to stderr.

--permissive
    Permit file access regardless of the policy decision — useful for
    testing rules before actually enforcing them.

--no-details
    On termination, fapolicyd normally writes a usage report with
    statistics and process/file details. This option suppresses the
    sensitive file/process names, keeping only the statistics.

sections.title: SIGNALS
sections.code:
SIGTERM   Halt event processing, write the performance report, and
          terminate.
SIGHUP    Reload the trust database.
SIGUSR1   Dump internal statistics to /var/run/fapolicyd.state.

sections.title: NOTES
sections.code:
DO NOT TRY TO ATTACH WITH PTRACE. Ptrace attachment sends a SIGSTOP
which cannot be blocked; if the continuation signal is never sent, the
system can deadlock, since core library access itself depends on
fapolicyd's approval.

Audit event generation requires auditing to be enabled and at least
one syscall audit rule loaded. RPM database trust sources should
minimize 32-bit packages, since identical pathnames across
architectures can cause trust-database mismatches and delays.

compiled.rules is the result of merging the component files in
/etc/fapolicyd/rules.d/. Run fapolicyd-cli --list to compare rule
numbers in debug output against the actual rule that triggered.

sections.title: FILES
sections.code:
/etc/fapolicyd/fapolicyd.conf       daemon configuration
/etc/fapolicyd/compiled.rules       access control rules
/etc/fapolicyd/fapolicyd.trust      admin-defined trusted files
/var/log/fapolicyd-access.log       access information log
/var/run/fapolicyd.state            internal performance metrics

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.code: fapolicyd-cli [options]

sections.title: DESCRIPTION
sections.code:
The fapolicyd-cli utility tells the daemon it needs to update the
trust database. The daemon normally learns about database updates via
a dnf plugin, but a manual RPM install or a direct edit to
fapolicyd.trust may not trigger that automatically — this utility
lets an administrator notify the daemon by hand when trust database
synchronization is needed.

sections.title: OPTIONS
sections.code:
-h, --help
    Print a list of command-line options.

--check-config
    Open fapolicyd.conf and parse it to check for syntax errors.

--check-path
    Check the PATH environment variable against the trust database,
    looking for a file not in the trustdb that could cause problems at
    run time.

--check-status
    Dump the daemon's internal performance statistics.

--check-trustdb
    Check the trustdb against the files on disk, looking for
    mismatches that would cause problems at run time.

--check-watch_fs
    Check mounted filesystems against the watch_fs config entry, to
    see if any filesystems need to be added.

-d, --delete-db
    Delete the trust database. Normally never needed, but it's the
    only recovery method if the trust database becomes corrupted.

-D, --dump-db
    Dump the trust database contents for inspection: original trust
    source, path, file size, and SHA256 sum for each entry.

-f, --file add|delete|update [path]
    Manage the file trust database.
    add: adds the file at path (size + SHA256 computed); if path is a
    directory, walks it to the bottom and adds every regular file
    found; by default appends to fapolicyd.trust.
    delete: deletes every entry matching path — can match multiple
    entries so a whole directory can be deleted in one command (end
    with '/' to match only a directory, not a partial name).
    update: refreshes the size/hash of matching paths — all files if
    no path is given, otherwise only matching ones (end with '/' to
    match a directory).

--trust-file trust-file-name
    Use after --file: makes every --file operation act on a single
    named trust file inside trust.d/, creating it if it doesn't exist.

-t, --ftype /path/to/file
    Print the MIME type fapolicyd assigns this file — helps get a
    rule's ftype parameter right. fapolicyd's classification can
    differ from the file(1) command's.

-l, --list
    List the fapolicyd rules file with a rule number, to help
    troubleshoot or interpret debug messages.

-u, --update
    Notify fapolicyd to update the trust database.

sections.code: fapolicyd(8), fapolicyd.rules(5), fapolicyd.trust(5), fapolicyd.conf(5)

purpose: fagenrules - a script that merges component fapolicyd rule files

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.code: fagenrules [--check] [--load]

sections.title: DESCRIPTION
sections.code:
fagenrules merges every component fapolicyd rules file found in
/etc/fapolicyd/rules.d/, placing the merged result in
/etc/fapolicyd/compiled.rules. Only files ending in ".rules" are
processed; everything else in that directory is ignored. Files are
concatenated in natural sort order with empty lines and comments
removed. compiled.rules is only rewritten if the merged content
actually differs from what's already there — the direct fapolicyd
counterpart of auditd's augenrules(8).

sections.title: OPTIONS
sections.code:
--check
    Test whether the rules have changed and would need updating,
    without actually modifying compiled.rules.

--load
    Load the existing or newly generated rules into the daemon.

sections.title: FILES
sections.code:
/etc/fapolicyd/rules.d/
/etc/fapolicyd/compiled.rules

sections.title: SEE ALSO
sections.code: fapolicyd.rules(5), fapolicyd-cli(8), fapolicyd(8)

sections.title: DESCRIPTION
sections.code:
/etc/fapolicyd/fapolicyd.conf holds the daemon's runtime performance
and behavior settings. One keyword per line, keyword = value; options
are case-insensitive, comments start with '#', and lines over 160
characters are skipped.

sections.title: CONFIGURATION OPTIONS
sections.code:
permissive (default 0)
    Enforcement mode: 0 sends policy decisions to the kernel for
    enforcement; 1 permits all access regardless of policy — testing
    only.

nice_val (default 10)
    Scheduler priority boost, 0-20.

q_size (default 800)
    Internal queue capacity for pending requests when demand exceeds
    fapolicyd's response rate. Affects file-descriptor allocation and
    should be coordinated with systemd's LimitNOFILE.

uid / gid (default 0 / 0)
    Numeric ID or account/group name the daemon runs as.

do_stat_report (default 1)
    Write a statistics report to /var/log/fapolicyd-access.log at
    shutdown.

detailed_report (default 1)
    Include subject/object cache details in that statistics report.

db_max_size (default 50)
    Maximum trust database size, in megabytes.

subj_cache_size (default 1549) / obj_cache_size (default 8191)
    Subject cache entry capacity (max 64k) / object cache entry
    capacity.

watch_fs (default ext4,xfs,tmpfs)
    Comma-separated filesystems to monitor, matching the names in
    /proc/mounts.

trust (default rpmdb,file)
    Comma-separated trust backends: file reads
    /etc/fapolicyd/fapolicyd.trust; rpmdb reads the RPM package
    database.

integrity (default none)
    Hash verification strategy: none, size, ima, or sha256.

syslog_format
    Comma-separated log fields drawn from the rule that matched, with
    a ':' separating subject from object keywords — e.g.
    rule,dec,perm,auid,pid,exe,:,path,ftype,trust. Limited to 512
    bytes.

rpm_sha256_only (default 0)
    Force SHA256-only hashing when set to 1 (otherwise SHA1 entries
    are also accepted).

allow_filesystem_mark (default 0)
    Permit monitoring bind-mounted or overlay filesystems when set to
    1.

sections.code: fapolicyd(8), fapolicyd-cli(8), fapolicyd.rules(5)

purpose: fapolicyd.rules / compiled.rules - the rules fapolicyd uses to determine access rights

sections.title: DESCRIPTION
sections.code:
compiled.rules, generated by fagenrules from /etc/fapolicyd/rules.d/,
holds the rules fapolicyd uses for access decisions. Format:

decision perm subject : object

Rules are evaluated in order; the first match wins. The ':' separator
between subject and object is mandatory, since the two sides share
some keywords (all, dir, ftype, trust).

sections.title: DECISION KEYWORDS
sections.code:
allow          permit the access
deny           block the access
allow_audit    permit and trigger a FANOTIFY audit event
deny_audit     block and trigger a FANOTIFY audit event
allow_syslog   permit and write to syslog
deny_syslog    block and write to syslog
allow_log      permit and generate both an audit event and a syslog entry
deny_log       block and generate both an audit event and a syslog entry

At least one audit rule must be loaded to actually generate an audit
event.

sections.title: PERMISSION TYPES (perm)
sections.code:
open       file access (the default if perm is unspecified)
execute    program execution
any        applies to any operation

sections.title: SUBJECT ATTRIBUTES
sections.code:
all
    Matches any subject — must be the only subject field in the rule.

auid
    Login UID assigned by the audit system; daemons carry -1. Numeric
    or account name.

uid / gid
    User/group ID running the program. Numeric or name.

sessionid
    Numeric audit session ID; daemons carry -1.

pid / ppid
    Process ID / parent process ID. Programs orphaned or started
    directly from systemd carry ppid=1; kernel threads carry ppid=2.

trust
    Boolean (1 or 0): whether the subject must exist in the trust
    database.

comm
    Shortened command name. When an interpreter starts a program, it
    usually renames the process to the script rather than the
    interpreter.

exe
    Full path to the executable — no globbing. The keyword untrusted
    matches processes not in the RPM database.

dir
    Directory match, recommended to end with '/'. Three built-in
    keywords: execdirs (/usr/, /bin/, /sbin/, /lib/, /lib64/,
    /usr/libexec/), systemdirs (execdirs plus /etc/), untrusted
    (executables not in the trust database — deprecated in favor of
    obj_trust).

ftype
    MIME type of the process's own executable. Use
    fapolicyd-cli --ftype /path to determine one.

device
    Device containing the executable, as /dev/<name>.

pattern
    Access pattern detected at program startup: normal (dynamically
    linked ELF), ld_so (started directly by the runtime linker),
    ld_preload (LD_PRELOAD/LD_AUDIT set in the environment), static
    (statically linked ELF).

sections.title: OBJECT ATTRIBUTES
sections.code:
all
    Matches any object — must be the only object field in the rule.

path
    Full path to the accessed file — no globbing. untrusted matches
    files not in the RPM database.

dir
    Directory match for the file — same execdirs/systemdirs/untrusted
    keywords as the subject's dir.

device
    Device containing the accessed file, as /dev/<name>.

ftype
    MIME type of the accessed file.

trust
    Boolean (1 or 0): whether the object must exist in the trust
    database.

sha256hash
    Matches the file's content hash — lowercase, no 0x prefix.

sections.title: SETS
sections.code:
A set is a named group of same-type values. Definition syntax:
%setname=value1,value2,... — the name starts with '%', then
alphanumerics/underscores; values are comma-separated; the internal
type (INT or STRING) is inferred from the first item. Sets can be used
for subject and object attributes, but not for trust or pattern.

%python=/usr/bin/python2.7,/usr/bin/python3.6
allow exe=%python : all trust=1

%uuids=0,1000
allow uid=%uuids : all

sections.title: EXAMPLES
sections.code:
deny_audit perm=open exe=/usr/bin/wget : dir=/tmp
allow perm=open exe=/usr/bin/python3.7 : ftype=text/x-python trust=1
deny_audit perm=any pattern=ld_so : all
deny perm=any all : all
